A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VARCO Arena and provide readable text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be reliably matched despite extensive rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original stochastic simulations and empirical GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini judging experiments, including rank correlations, insertion errors, and uncertainty analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds empirical comparisons using Claude, Llama, Qwen, and Gemma judges in Table 3.

M1.justification: The method still randomizes single-elimination tournaments across prompts and aggregates match outcomes into Elo ratings. Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the tournament and binary-search procedures; the rewritten pseudocode and explanations do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Chatbot Arena-derived simulation inputs and the same Arena-Hard-Auto prompt/response collection, including the newcomer-insertion scenario. V2 mentions AlpacaEval as an alternative and multimodal evaluation as future work, without evaluating either.

E2.justification: Tournament ranking remains compared with reference-based win rates, and binary-search insertion remains compared with reference-based insertion. The additional LLMs serve as judges within these comparisons. No additional competing benchmarking algorithm is evaluated.

E3.justification: The empirical judge configurations expand from GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini to include Claude3.5-Sonnet, Llama3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-0.5B, and Gemma2-2B, evaluated with 500 prompts. This substantially broadens evaluation conditions across model families and sizes. The original prompt-count sweep, metrics, and simulation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 3 substantially extends robustness testing beyond the GPT judge family, examining whether the tournament advantage survives different judge families and capacities. It adds evidence of failure with very small judges. Existing simulation sensitivity tests, insertion experiments, and appendix separability analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 simulation trials, 500 empirical trials, and retained appendix analyses using 1,000 bootstrap samples and 95% confidence intervals. The caching and statistical-budget description moves to Appendix A.2. No new uncertainty-estimation practice or explicit increase in runs is reported.

E6.justification: Existing GPT score tables, insertion results, and appendix plots are unchanged. New Table 3 adds substantive findings: tournament/reference correlations are 0.930/0.924 for Claude3.5-Sonnet, 0.850/0.820 for Llama3.1-8B, and 0.811/0.756 for Qwen2.5-7B. The ordering reverses for Qwen2.5-0.5B (-0.124/0.089) and Gemma2-2B (0.552/0.592), establishing new exceptions to the favorable trend.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the earlier O(|X|/log2(nmodel)) comparison-budget argument with counting claims about |X| times nmodel/2 initial matches and a minimum of |X|/[2(nmodel−1)] matches per pair. Approximate prompt equivalence becomes explicit prompt independence. These substantially revise the assumptions and mathematical rationale, although Equations 1–3 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 adds demo and code release as an explicit third contribution in the introduction and announces it in the abstract. The central claims of reference-free ranking, fewer comparisons, and closer agreement with human-established Elo rankings remain substantially the same.

C2.justification: V2 recommends specialized judges or generative judges around 7B parameters after the small-model failures, and adds limitations concerning bracket randomness and better matchmaking. It removes v1's warning about combining disparate capabilities into one Elo rating and its two explanations for unstable binary-search insertion.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds A100 hardware information for open-weight inference. V2 describes the insertion reference more specifically as the top-performing model, while retaining the numerical results. It omits v1's dated GPT judge identifiers and explicit judge-exclusion statement. The new demo/code-release announcement supplies only an unresolved URL placeholder.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to the GPT-4o, Llama 3, Qwen2.5, and Gemma 2 reports, while removing Dynabench, the WMT23 metrics-task report, and MetricX-23. Related-work discussion is shortened, but the principal positioning around Elo ranking and reference-free evaluation remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, method rationale, experiments, discussion, and related work are rewritten. Sections 3.1 and 3.2 exchange order, experimental subsections are reorganized, the caching discussion moves to the appendix, a Limitations section is added, and the reproducibility checklist is removed.

P2.justification: V2 changes document-wide typesetting and column layout, adds the comparison-budget table and multi-judge results table, and revises plot legends and captions. Figure 1 moves to the first page; Figures 5–6 become stacked beside Algorithm 2. The numbered prompt code listing becomes ordinary formatted text. Most retained figures display the same underlying results.

improvement.justification: Table 3 broadens empirical support and exposes useful judge-capacity limitations, while the reorganization improves readability. However, v2 replaces a heuristic rationale with an unsupported per-pair coverage guarantee that randomized brackets do not ensure, removes an Elo applicability caveat and precise judge identifiers, and announces code release through a placeholder. These empirical gains and theoretical/documentation regressions leave the net quality improvement uncertain.
